fair_value_reason: P/E leg: FY28 SBC-inclusive EPS about $25.8 (FY27 $23.0, revenue +8-9%, modest leverage, about 5% net share reduction at current prices) x 12.5x = about $322. FCF leg: normalized FY28 SBC-burdened FCF about $6.3B on about 250M average shares = about $25.2/share at 8% = about $315, less about $2/share net debt. Blend about $320, vs the revised agents' mean of $316 and my round-1 $318.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged: fair values $310-328 (mean $316), P(>=$268 in a year) 0.535-0.575, thesis breaks $185-200. Almost all of that movement came from the agents adopting round-1 findings (normalized FCF, HRB at 6.6x, TurboTax share loss), not from new evidence. The one new primary fact is that buybacks are more accretive than anyone modeled: FY26 net employee issuance was only about 1% of shares, so $5-6B a year at about $270 cuts the count about 5% net. That lifts fair value to about $320 and the middle of the ladder by about a point. INTU is cheap at about 11.6x FY27 SBC-inclusive EPS, but the left tail stays fat until the Jan-Apr 2027 tax season shows whether TurboTax share loss continues.
key_drivers: FY27 guide reaffirmed Sep 17: revenue +9-10% (TurboTax +2-3%, GBS +13-14%), non-GAAP EPS $22.88-23.12 including about $5.81 of SBC; $268 is about 11.6x.

Buybacks are more accretive than modeled: FY26 net employee issuance was only 2.6M shares against 13.4M repurchased (-3.8% count at about $409 average). At about $270, $5-6B a year retires about 5-6% net, supporting FY28 EPS of about $25.8.
FY26 OCF includes a one-off $1.28B OBBBA deferred-tax benefit (about $0.7B more in FY27); normalized SBC-burdened FCF is about $5.3B, or about a 7.5% yield.
TurboTax lost about 3.7 points of relative share in the 2026 season (units -2% vs IRS self-prepared e-file +1.7%), and the HRB comparable is at about 6.6x. The 2027 season decides the left tail.
QBO list prices rose on Aug 1, 2026 (Plus $140, Advanced $340): an ARPC tailwind with churn risk, with online paying customers up only 3% in FY26.
